enonce_markdown: A trader in Mokolo market buys a bag of rice for 18,000 FCFA and sells it for 21,600 FCFA. What is his gross profit on the bag?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Gross profit on one item = selling price - cost price.

### Solution

Gross profit = 21,600 - 18,000 = 3,600 FCFA.

The figure 18,000 is the cost price and 39,600 adds the two prices together, which has no meaning.

**Answer: b.**

enonce_markdown: A shop buys a generator for 60,000 FCFA and sells it for 75,000 FCFA. Calculate the mark-up as a percentage of cost price.
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Mark-up (%) = gross profit / cost price x 100. It is based on the cost price, not on the selling price.

### Solution

Gross profit = 75,000 - 60,000 = 15,000 FCFA.

Mark-up = 15,000 / 60,000 x 100 = **25 %**.

The 20 % option is 15,000 / 75,000 x 100, which is the margin (based on the selling price). 80 % is cost divided by selling price.

**Answer: c.**

enonce_markdown: A wholesaler in Douala has opening stock of 4,500,000 FCFA, purchases of 9,000,000 FCFA, closing stock of 2,500,000 FCFA and net sales of 15,000,000 FCFA. What is his gross profit?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Cost of goods sold = opening stock + purchases - closing stock. Gross profit = net sales - cost of goods sold.

### Solution

Cost of goods sold = 4,500,000 + 9,000,000 - 2,500,000 = 11,000,000 FCFA.

Gross profit = 15,000,000 - 11,000,000 = **4,000,000 FCFA**.

Wrong answers: 6,000,000 ignores both stocks; 1,500,000 forgets to subtract the closing stock; 11,000,000 is the cost of goods sold, not the profit.

**Answer: a.**

enonce_markdown: A boutique in Bamenda adds a mark-up of 30 % on cost price. A dress costs the boutique 25,000 FCFA. What is its selling price?
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Mark-up is a percentage of the cost price. Selling price = cost price + (mark-up % x cost price) = cost price x (1 + mark-up/100).

### Solution

Mark-up = 30/100 x 25,000 = 7,500 FCFA.

Selling price = 25,000 + 7,500 = **32,500 FCFA**.

35,714 FCFA comes from treating 30 % as a percentage of the selling price (a margin), and 25,030 comes from adding 30 FCFA instead of 30 %.

**Answer: c.**

enonce_markdown:
The following figures are taken from the books of Ngu Stores for the year.

| Item | FCFA |
|---|---:|
| Net sales | 9,600,000 |
| Opening stock | 1,200,000 |
| Purchases | 6,800,000 |
| Closing stock | 1,600,000 |
| Wages | 900,000 |
| Rent | 480,000 |
| Transport | 220,000 |

Calculate: (a) the cost of goods sold; (b) the gross profit; (c) the net profit; (d) the mark-up as a percentage of cost of goods sold.

(8 marks)
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Cost of goods sold = opening stock + purchases - closing stock. Gross profit = sales - cost of goods sold. Net profit = gross profit - expenses. Mark-up = gross profit / cost of goods sold x 100.

### Solution

**(a)** Cost of goods sold = 1,200,000 + 6,800,000 - 1,600,000 = **6,400,000 FCFA**.

**(b)** Gross profit = 9,600,000 - 6,400,000 = **3,200,000 FCFA**.

**(c)** Expenses = 900,000 + 480,000 + 220,000 = 1,600,000 FCFA. Net profit = 3,200,000 - 1,600,000 = **1,600,000 FCFA**.

**(d)** Mark-up = 3,200,000 / 6,400,000 x 100 = **50 %**.

enonce_markdown:
A hardware shop in Garoua prices all its goods at a mark-up of 40 % on cost. During one month its sales at these prices total 2,800,000 FCFA.

(a) Calculate the cost of goods sold.

(b) Calculate the gross profit and the gross margin (profit as a percentage of sales, to 2 decimal places).

(c) A new competitor forces the shop to cut every selling price by 10 %. If the same goods had been sold at the reduced prices, calculate the new gross profit and the new mark-up on cost.

(d) State by how many percentage points the mark-up has fallen, and say why the fall is not just 10 points.

(8 marks)
corrige_markdown:
### Method reminder

Selling price = cost x (1 + mark-up/100), so cost = selling price / (1 + mark-up/100). Margin is based on sales, mark-up on cost. After a price cut the cost is unchanged, so profit falls by the whole amount of the cut.

### Solution

**(a)** Cost of goods sold = 2,800,000 / 1.40 = **2,000,000 FCFA**.

**(b)** Gross profit = 2,800,000 - 2,000,000 = **800,000 FCFA**. Gross margin = 800,000 / 2,800,000 x 100 = **28.57 %**.

**(c)** New sales = 90 % of 2,800,000 = 2,520,000 FCFA. The cost is unchanged at 2,000,000 FCFA, so new gross profit = 2,520,000 - 2,000,000 = **520,000 FCFA**. New mark-up = 520,000 / 2,000,000 x 100 = **26 %**.

**(d)** The mark-up fell from 40 % to 26 %, a fall of **14 percentage points**. The whole 280,000 FCFA price cut comes off the profit because the cost does not change; this is why the profit fell by 280,000 FCFA, from 800,000 to 520,000 FCFA (a drop of 35 % of the profit).
